text:
Maria G: ok team — planning thread for integrating FlashAttention v2/v3. Goal: safe perf uplift >v2 on short/med seq while keeping paged-attn KV stability for long contexts. Need kernel selection rules, feature-flag strategy, and canary playbook.

Aj Patel: quick note: last canary showed a regression on KV-heavy traces (1k+ tokens). p95 latency up ~7% with v3 default kernel. profiling attached below.

Aj Patel: profiler snippet:```
MODEL: redwood-base-13b
CONFIG: batch=32, seq=1024, kv_paged=true
kernel=v3_fused : p50=98ms p95=210ms
kernel=v2_legacy: p50=105ms p95=196ms
notes: v3 wins in small seqs but suffers with paged KV warmups
```

Kai L: thanks. proposal: adaptive chooser based on two heuristics — "seq_len" and "kv_activity". Simple rule: if seq_len <= 512 -> prefer v3_fused. if seq_len > 512 and kv_activity > 0.6 -> prefer v2_paged_fallback. Use a soft-start flag to let chooser learn traffic distribution.

Maria G: sounds good. what about batching heuristics? continuous batching seems to amplify v3 wins but also increases memory pressure during paged evictions.

Aj Patel: from benching: increase max_batch to 48 for short tails (seq<=256) gives 12% throughput gain. For longer seqs, cap at 16 and enable early-eviction window for KV (ttl=30s) to avoid page thrash.

Ryan O: on the regression: I traced a hot path — decoder_kv_fetch on v3 has a misaligned prefetch during page faults, causing extra device-to-host hops. patch landed on branch "kv-prefetch-fix" reduces the extra hops. recommend adding that to canary bundle.

Kai L: feature-flag plan: create 3 flags -> `ff/attn/chooser` (controls adaptive chooser on/off), `ff/attn/v3_default` (toggle v3 as default), `ff/attn/kv_prefetch_fix` (controls the runtime patch). Rollout stages: 0% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with telemetry gates at each step (p50/p95, error rate, OOMs, evictions/sec).

Maria G: deploy-bot — can we gate by model-tag + route? we only want to target non-enterprise routes for initial canary.

deploy-bot: deploy requested: bundle=flashblend-chooser-2026-03-18, flags=[ff/attn/kv_prefetch_fix=true, ff/attn/chooser=true], target=nonprod and 2% prod routes. Status: canary started on 8 nodes. :rocket:

Aj Patel: perf telemetry to watch: 1) p95 latency delta per model/version 2) evictions/sec 3) cpu-gpu memcpy counters 4) failed page reads. I'll add dashboards and an alert if p95 increases >5% vs baseline for >10m.

Kai L: ops checklist for canary:
- start with 2% traffic for 1h, check telemetry
- enable kv_prefetch_fix flag only after 2% stable
- if evictions/sec spikes >2x, rollback chooser flag
- collect traces for 100 slowest requests and attach to ticket

Ryan O: if we hit regressions, fallback: force `kernel=v2_legacy` via route override and kill canary. Also add a runtime fallback to detect page-fault spikes and auto-switch kernels for affected requests.

Maria G: action items: Aj -> dashboards + baseline runs. Kai -> implement chooser config and flag gating logic. Ryan -> promote kv-prefetch-fix to canary bundle and confirm no regressions on long-context synthetic tests. I'll coordinate rollout with support/CS.

Aj Patel: baseline numbers I'll post in the #perf channel after runs. initial microbench shows +18% tokens/sec on 128/256 seqs with v3+chooser.

Maria G: perfect. tagging @Kai L @Ryan O — let's meet in 30m to lock timing. :thumbsup:
